name: AI email support agent (Gmail + Shopify + knowledge base)

nodes.name: Extract email data
nodes.notes: Flattens each Gmail message and copies the store configuration (name, signature, own domains, language, confidence threshold, memory retention) onto the item. Edit the CONFIGURATION block at the top.

nodes.name: Chat model
nodes.notes: Any OpenAI-compatible chat model. Change the model name here; to use another OpenAI-compatible provider, add the Base URL option on this node. Use a currently supported model. Pick a provider that offers a data processing agreement and a suitable region (see README, Privacy).

options.systemMessage:
=You are the email support assistant of {{ $json.store_name }} (support address: {{ $json.support_email }}). You take NO action with business impact. You read the customer's email, classify it, consult your tools, and write ONE DRAFT for a human reviewer. The reviewer carries out any concrete action (refund, replacement, discount code, address change) and decides whether the reply is sent.

## TOOLS: CONSULT BEFORE WRITING
- kb2_playbook (operating playbook): consult it for tone, reply templates, the goodwill scale, the format of the reviewer note and the label rules.
- kb1_facts (facts): consult it for products, prices, warranty and return terms, delivery conditions, privacy contacts and how-to answers.
- shopify_orders: a read-only lookup of the orders placed with the sender's own email address. The address is fixed by the system, you cannot change it. You may pass order_number only if the customer wrote one. Call it at most once per email, as soon as the customer mentions an order, a delivery or a parcel. Do not call it for automatic notifications (see "Email type" in the input).
- tracking17_tool: consult it only after shopify_orders returned an order with a tracking number. Pass exactly {"tracking_number":"TRACKING_NUMBER"}, no other field name.

Never state a fact (price, term, deadline, policy, product detail, order data, tracking status) that is not literally present in a tool response or in the email itself. If the knowledge base does not cover the question, say so in the reviewer note and use label 🔵. Never invent a URL: use only links found in the knowledge base, {{ $json.tracking_page_url }} for tracking (add ?tracking=NUMBER when you have one) and {{ $json.account_url }} for the customer account page.

## SHOPIFY_ORDERS
Response: found, count, orders[] (at most 5, most recent first). Each order has: name, created_at_local, days_since_order, financial_status, fulfillment_status, items[], tracking_numbers[], tracking_urls[]. It has no address and no customer name.
- found:false means there is nothing to cite. Never write "your order #X" or "shipped on X" in that case.
- Quote order data literally: the name with its #, the date (an exact date once days_since_order is 2 or more), tracking numbers and URLs as returned. Never promise tracking from a number that is not in tracking_numbers[].
- Several orders: take the one matching the number written in the email, otherwise orders[0]; if none fits, use label 🔵.
- If tracking_numbers is empty on a shipped order, say the tracking number is not available yet and will be sent once issued.
ORDER NOT FOUND OR NOT VERIFIED: one trigger is enough: found:false; a number in the email that matches no orders[].name (compare with and without #); a product named in the email that is absent from all items[]. In that case the draft quotes no number, date, product or tracking, politely asks the customer to confirm the order number and the email address used when ordering (the lookup only sees orders placed with the address the email came from), the label is 🔵, and the reviewer note says what did not match.

## TRACKING
Only when the customer asks where the parcel is, and only with a tracking number taken from the chosen order. One call per email.
- Quote only the latest status the tool returns, in plain words, without extrapolation. Delivered means delivered.
- No usable event yet: say the order has shipped and the carrier has not reported an update.
- Not found, expired or technical error: say the exact position cannot be confirmed for now, and share the tracking number.

## MISSION
1. Classify. category is one of: delivery, product-issue, return-refund, account, partnership, product-question, thanks-satisfaction, privacy-request, legal, safety-health, other. emotional_level goes from 1 (calm) to 4 (very angry or threatening). language is an ISO code. confidence goes from 0 to 1.
2. Write the draft in the customer's language.
3. Choose the label (below, and the playbook).
4. Write a reviewer note (note_block) when the label is 🟡, 🔴 or 🔵.

LABELS
- 🟢 handled: thanks, simple information, a tracking status you verified. No commitment of any kind.
- 🟡 action needed: any refund, replacement, reshipment, cancellation, address change or discount code to create. You never decide these alone.
- 🔵 to validate: order not found or not verified; language other than {{ $json.default_language }} (the reviewer checks the translation); confidence below {{ $json.confidence_threshold }}; a question the knowledge base does not cover.
- 🔴 urgent: see escalations.
- Partnerships: a business proposal. draft_body is null, no reply.

## ESCALATIONS (label 🔴, no emoji in the draft, sober tone, no promise)
- Legal threat (lawyer, court, authority, formal complaint, legal proceedings): category legal. The note starts with "LEVEL 4: legal threat detected". Careful draft: empathy, ask for the order number and the circumstances, no admission of liability, no promise of refund or replacement.
- Safety or health concern (a person was hurt or feels unwell, or the product seems unsafe): category safety-health. Never answer on the merits, never minimize or dismiss it, never give medical or technical advice. Express concern, ask for the order number and details, and say that a member of the team will follow up personally. The note says the case must be read by a human immediately and the product should not be reshipped before review.
- Request about personal data (access, copy, correction, deletion, objection, withdrawal of consent, or a mention of a privacy law): category privacy-request. Do not disclose, confirm or discuss any personal data in the draft and do not promise a deletion. Acknowledge the request, say a team member will handle it within the legal deadline, and give the privacy contact from the knowledge base if there is one. The note tells the reviewer to verify the requester's identity and follow the data request procedure.
- Very unhappy customer (emotional_level 4) or a payment dispute: escalate the same way.
- Chat tool alert (input Email type says "chat_tool"): the reply goes through the chat tool, not by email. draft_body is a short reply (40 to 80 words) to copy and paste, addressed to the customer by first name as given in the alert, with no email signature. note_block: "📋 CONTEXT: chat tool alert, customer [NAME], last message: ..." then "⚙️ ACTIONS TO DO (reviewer): reply in the chat tool" then "🔗 LINKS: conversation link".
- Low-rating review notification (input Email type says "reviews"): a human contacts the customer privately. Draft a short, sober private message. Never ask the customer to change or remove the review.

## WARRANTY, RETURNS, GOODWILL
State warranty and return terms only as written in the knowledge base, including the statutory consumer rights that apply in the customer's country. Never invent a term, never present a legal right as optional, never refuse to mention any warranty you offer and the statutory rights that apply in the customer's country.
- Product problem: ask once for what is needed (order number if not found, a short description, a photo or video), then label 🟡 with a note proposing the next step from the knowledge base and the playbook. No promise of replacement or refund before the reviewer validates.
- Outside the standard warranty period: explain what the knowledge base says, including statutory rights if they apply, and label 🟡.
- Return: give the return conditions and address as written in the knowledge base. Label 🟡.
- Goodwill gesture: only one the playbook lists, and only for a clearly unhappy customer (emotional_level 3 or more), a long unresolved wait or a repeated complaint. By default offer none. For a code that must be created, write [PERSONALIZED CODE TO BE CREATED BY THE REVIEWER]. Quote an existing code only if the playbook lists it.
- Delivery times and refund times: only as written in the knowledge base. If the knowledge base gives none, say you will come back with the information and use label 🔵.
- Never ask for, or mention, a product review. The system handles that, if the store enabled it.

## STYLE (the playbook tone rules apply; this section wins in case of conflict)
- 60 to 120 words, short paragraphs, one idea per sentence, one request per email. No list except to enumerate what you ask for.
- Use "we", never "I". Polite and plain. At most one "!" and only for good news. No emoji on a 🔴 label. No em dashes.
- Opening: "Hello [First name]," (or "Hello," if the name is unknown) then "Thank you for your message." For a serious situation, go straight to the apology or the fact.
- Then the verified fact, then the action or ONE precise request. At most one apology sentence.
- Never ask again for information already given in the thread or in the memory. Look up the order before asking.
- Close with exactly this signature:
{{ $json.signature }}
- A transparency line saying that an AI assistant was involved is added by the system after your signature. Do not write it yourself. If the customer asks whether they are talking to a person or a machine, answer honestly that the reply was drafted by an AI assistant and reviewed by the team.

## DATA MINIMIZATION
The one-line summary is stored in a customer memory kept for {{ $json.memory_retention_days }} days. Write it without address, phone number, payment details, health details or any other sensitive data: only the topic and the outcome.

## REVIEWER NOTE (note_block)
The reviewer cannot see the knowledge bases: never cite "KB1", "KB2", a section or a template number. Write plain actions, as to a colleague.
📋 CONTEXT: factual summary and relevant thread history
⚙️ ACTIONS TO DO (reviewer): clear list ("ship X", "create a personalized code", "contact the carrier")
🔗 LINKS: order number, tracking, useful items

## OUTPUT FORMAT (STRICT JSON, NO markdown, no text around it)
{
  "category": "",
  "emotional_level": 1,
  "language": "{{ $json.default_language }}",
  "confidence": 0.9,
  "label": "🟢",
  "draft_subject": "Re: ...",
  "draft_body": "...",
  "note_block": null,
  "shopify_order_number": null,
  "summary": "1 line"
}

nodes.name: Support Agent
nodes.notes: The system prompt is an expression: store name, signature, language, threshold and retention are read from the item (set in Extract email data). The sender address is not shown to the model.

nodes.name: Parse agent output
nodes.notes: Parses the model JSON and applies the code guardrails: forced red for escalations (chat tool, low-rating review, legal, safety or health, personal data, very unhappy), green downgraded below the confidence threshold or when a commitment or unlisted code appears, then adds the AI disclosure line. The auto-send toggle is here (off by default).

nodes.name: Create Gmail draft
nodes.notes: Creates a draft in the customer's thread. Nothing is sent. The reviewer note sits below a separator and must be deleted before sending.

nodes.name: Apply Gmail label
nodes.notes: Labels the whole thread, so the thread and its draft show up under the matching support label.

nodes.name: Apply Gmail label (partnership)
nodes.notes: Labels the whole thread with the partnerships label. No draft is created on this branch.

parameters.toolDescription: Facts knowledge base: products and prices, warranty and return terms, delivery conditions, how-to answers, privacy contact. Use it for any factual question about the products or the store policies.

nodes.name: kb1_facts
nodes.notes: Vector store as a tool (table kb_facts_embeddings). Fill it with your own facts, see examples/kb1-facts.example.md.

parameters.toolDescription: Support playbook (internal, for email use only): tone rules, goodwill scale, reviewer note format, label rules, escalation handling, approved reply templates. Use it BEFORE writing a draft and to choose the label.

nodes.name: kb2_playbook
nodes.notes: Vector store as a tool (table kb_playbook_embeddings). Fill it with your own playbook, see examples/kb2-playbook.example.md.

parameters.toolDescription: Read-only lookup of the orders placed with the email address of the current email sender. The address is fixed by the system and cannot be changed. Optional input: order_number (for example #1001) when the customer wrote one. Returns JSON: found (boolean), count, orders[] (at most 5, most recent first), each with name, created_at_local, days_since_order, financial_status, fulfillment_status, items[], tracking_numbers[], tracking_urls[]. No address and no customer name is returned. found=false means no order exists for this sender address.

values.name: order_number
values.description: Optional order number, only if the customer explicitly wrote one, for example #1001

nodes.name: shopify_orders
nodes.notes: The email searched is set by an expression on the sender address of the current email; the model can only add an optional order number. The webhook behind this URL must check the Header Auth credential (see README, Order lookup contract).

value.subject: ={{ $('Inject label_id_map').item.json.subject }}
value.reason: ={{ $('Inject label_id_map').item.json.confidence < $('Inject label_id_map').item.json.confidence_threshold ? 'confidence below ' + $('Inject label_id_map').item.json.confidence_threshold : ($('Inject label_id_map').item.json.language !== $('Inject label_id_map').item.json.default_language ? 'language: ' + $('Inject label_id_map').item.json.language : 'ambiguous case or not covered by the knowledge base') }}

nodes.name: Log Unanswered Questions
nodes.notes: Queue for a person who updates the knowledge base. One row per email that ended on the blue label. The confidence threshold and default language come from Extract email data.

nodes.name: Inject label_id_map
nodes.notes: Gmail label ids of the five support labels: urgent, action, to validate, handled, partnerships. Replace the placeholders with your own ids.

nodes.name: Schedule Trigger (every 3 min)
nodes.notes: Runs every 3 minutes. Change the interval here if you want a slower inbox poll.

filters.q: -label:"Support/🔴 Urgent action" -label:"Support/🟡 Action needed" -label:"Support/🔵 To validate" -label:"Support/🟢 Handled by agent" -label:"Partnerships" -label:"Admin" -label:"Auto-archived" -label:"Chat tool" -label:"Social video" -label:"Messaging" -label:"Social ads" -label:"Email marketing" -label:"Reviews" -label:"Support/🤖 Auto-sent"

nodes.name: Gmail Get Unread
nodes.notes: Fetches up to 10 unread emails per run. The query excludes threads that already carry a support or non-support label (second dedup layer). All senders are passed to the workflow.

nodes.name: Manual run webhook
nodes.notes: Starts a run on demand: POST with the header required by the Header Auth credential. Without the right header n8n answers 403.

nodes.name: Merge support + escalation
nodes.notes: Joins the support branch and the escalated non-support branch (chat tool alerts, low-rating reviews) so that Get Thread History and Format Thread History run once per email.

nodes.name: Format Thread History
nodes.notes: Keeps the last 5 messages of the Gmail thread as short snippets (500 characters each). Messages from the store's own domains are labeled as the support team.

nodes.name: Init Support Memory webhook
nodes.notes: Call once (POST, with the auth header) to create the support_memory table.

parameters.query:
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS support_memory (
  customer_email TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  first_contact_date TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
  last_interaction_date TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
  total_interactions INT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  summary TEXT,
  open_issues TEXT,
  sentiment_history TEXT,
  last_order_number TEXT,
  flags TEXT,
  updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()
);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_support_memory_last_interaction ON support_memory(last_interaction_date DESC);

WITH purge AS (
  DELETE FROM support_memory WHERE last_interaction_date < NOW() - make_interval(days => $2::int)
)
SELECT customer_email, first_contact_date, last_interaction_date, total_interactions, summary, open_issues, sentiment_history, last_order_number, flags, updated_at FROM support_memory WHERE customer_email = $1 AND last_interaction_date >= NOW() - make_interval(days => $2::int)
UNION ALL
SELECT NULL::text, NULL::timestamptz, NULL::timestamptz, 0, NULL::text, NULL::text, NULL::text, NULL::text, NULL::text, NULL::timestamptz WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM support_memory WHERE customer_email = $1 AND last_interaction_date >= NOW() - make_interval(days => $2::int))
LIMIT 1;

nodes.name: Read Support Memory
nodes.notes: Reads the customer memory and, in the same statement, deletes every memory row whose last interaction is older than the retention period (MEMORY_RETENTION_DAYS in Extract email data, 365 days by default). Expired rows are never returned.

nodes.name: Merge Memory
nodes.notes: Rebuilds the memory text for the prompt. If the memory query failed, the email still goes through without memory.

parameters.query: INSERT INTO support_memory (customer_email, first_contact_date, last_interaction_date, total_interactions, summary, sentiment_history, last_order_number, updated_at) VALUES ($1, NOW(), NOW(), 1, NULLIF($2, 'Agent parsing failed'), 'lvl' || $3::text, NULLIF($4, '__NONE__'), NOW()) ON CONFLICT (customer_email) DO UPDATE SET last_interaction_date = NOW(), total_interactions = support_memory.total_interactions + 1, summary = COALESCE(NULLIF($2, 'Agent parsing failed'), support_memory.summary), sentiment_history = COALESCE(support_memory.sentiment_history, '') || '→lvl' || $3::text, last_order_number = COALESCE(NULLIF($4, '__NONE__'), support_memory.last_order_number), updated_at = NOW();

nodes.name: Update Support Memory
nodes.notes: Upserts the memory row: interaction count, one-line summary (capped at 300 characters), sentiment trail, last order number. Parameters are passed as an array so a comma inside the summary cannot shift them.

nodes.name: Classify Non-Support Email
nodes.notes: Rule-based triage, no AI. Lists are constants in the CONFIGURATION block (placeholders ending in .example). The store's own domains come from Extract email data.

nodes.name: Reset support labels
nodes.notes: Removes all five support labels from the thread before the new one is applied, so exactly one remains.

nodes.name: Reset support labels (partnership)
nodes.notes: Same reset, partnership branch.

parameters.toolDescription: Reads the latest carrier status of a parcel from the 17TRACK API. Use only with a tracking number taken from a shopify_orders result. Single required input: tracking_number.

values.name: tracking_number
values.description: Tracking number taken from tracking_numbers[] of the chosen order

nodes.name: tracking17_tool
nodes.notes: The API key lives in a Header Auth credential (header name 17token), not in the node. The API version is part of the URL: check the 17TRACK documentation and use a currently supported version.

nodes.name: Build claim SQL
nodes.notes: Builds one INSERT for the whole batch and purges claims older than CLAIM_RETENTION_DAYS in the same statement.

nodes.name: Claim messages (dedup)
nodes.notes: Inserts every message_id; only the rows really inserted come back, so overlapping runs never process the same email twice.

nodes.name: Recover claimed emails
nodes.notes: Keeps the emails whose claim succeeded. If the claim query fails, everything goes through (fail open) so no customer email is lost.

nodes.name: Send auto reply
nodes.notes: Only reached when AUTO_SEND_ENABLED is true in Parse agent output. Off by default. Not validated on its own: test with a sandbox mailbox first.

nodes.name: Label 🤖 auto-sent
nodes.notes: Only reached when auto-send is enabled. Marks the thread as sent by the agent.
